correctness.rationale: C PASS: For a centered apex over [-a,a] x [-b,b], every apex-to-base path must enter the base through some edge. Its two segments have lower bound |v-q|+|p-q|, attained by a lateral-face straight chord followed by the base segment. Unfolding across each of four actual edges yields sites (+/-C_a,0),(0,+/-C_b); the straight image segment crosses inside the edge because C_a-x>=sqrt(h^2+a^2) and similarly on y edges. The four-site distance minimum is therefore globally exact, with no unexamined multi-face path. Bisector equations C_a x-C_b y=aC_a-bC_b produce the H-shaped Voronoi cut locus, branch nodes (+/-u,0), u=a-bC_b/C_a; at a=b they merge. Convex squared distance on each Voronoi cell reduces farthest-point candidates to its vertices. The branch-node squared distance exceeds the corner/lateral maximum by 2b sqrt(h^2+b^2)(sqrt(h^2+a^2)+bC_b/C_a)/C_a>0, so exactly the branch nodes maximize. L=2a-2bt+4b sqrt(1+t^2); t increases from b/a to 1 and derivative changes at t=1/sqrt(3). This proves the strict threshold a/b>sqrt(3), unique h_*^2=3a^2+3b^2-4sqrt(3)ab and min L=2a+2sqrt(3)b, with square constant case. Independent calculation compared the four-site maximum on 10,004 base grid locations in four parameter sets. Grid sampling is only corroboration, not proof.
